dictionary.definition: How much weight each type carries given the unit's democracy score alone, with state authority and state capacity unobserved. The six weights add to 1. This is not a classification: tested on the 3,476 classified country-years with both state measures hidden, the democracy score alone identifies the right type 59% of the time, and two of the six types are never the largest weight at any democracy score.

Holding the democracy score fixed and letting state authority and state capacity take every value between 0 and 1, these are the types that win somewhere. A type absent from this list is ruled out whatever the state measures would have shown. This uses no prior and no judgement, and is the firmer of the two results.

The share of the authority by capacity square each type wins, under a uniform prior over that square. These are areas, not probabilities. Across all 304 unit-years the largest share runs only 0.25 to 0.53, so no unit is close to determined by area. The largest share is not a most likely type and can disagree with the posterior: Somaliland's posterior favors Weak Authoritarian while the largest area belongs to Less-Capable Hybrid.

Which type would apply at each combination of state authority and capacity, at the unit's last covered year. Read the region matching what is known about the case, not the largest region. Gaza is the standing example: averaged over the whole square its largest weight sits on a high-authority type, which vanishes entirely along the low-authority edge where the case actually sits.
The fewest types whose weights add to 0.90. A display convenience only. Two units 0.2 apart on the democracy score can receive identical sets, so the full distribution is the deliverable.

libdem_observed: the democracy score is measured and both state measures are absent. libdem_bridged_FH: Tibet, whose democracy score is predicted from a frozen Freedom House crosswalk. posterior_mix_WB_Gaza: the combined Palestine line, which mixes the West Bank and Gaza distributions at fixed weights of 0.60 and 0.40 and therefore has no single democracy score of its own.

Whether the unit was in an episode of regime change that year, from V-Dem's Episodes of Regime Transformation. Stable is a residual category meaning not currently inside an episode, not that nothing is moving. Blank for Tibet, which is not a V-Dem unit.

Units absent from the state fragility data throughout, and units covered for only part of 2004-2024. The partially covered countries are classified in their remaining years and appear in the main panel there. Tibet is covered from 2012, when the Freedom House series begins.
